intro: Creating local networks that reduce food waste while strengthening neighborhood relationships and practical solidarity.

body.heading: Purpose
body.text:
Our food system is broken. Currently, it is the primarly driver for the transgression of our planetary boundaries. In Finland alone, 1.1 tons of edible food is thrown away every single day (Natural Resources Institute Finland). 

**Ultimately, the question is not whether we transition away from the current system but rather how and to where?**

 For the past 3 years, I have worked on food system change from the end of the value chain, focusing on the reduction of food waste through Aalto Foodsharing in Finland. We are an initiative at the intersection of community-led grassroots action, public awareness, and political advocacy. Our goal is to become a global movement in tackling food waste.

body.heading: Operations
body.text:
I am mainly responsible for overseeing, improving and expanding our day-to-day operations, including managing our volunteer network and relationships with food business partners.

This is where my background in service design becomes particularly relevant. I identify challenges and develope practical solutions to adress them. This involves, for example questions of: 

→  How can we improve the onboarding experience for new volunteers? 
→ How can we make the food pick-up process smoother and more efficient for both volunteers and food suppliers?
→ How can we better reach and engage new food business partners through, for example, tailored information materials and introductory packages? 
→ And how can we ensure that our community fridge spaces remain clean, accessible and well-maintained?

body.heading: Outreach & Advocacy
body.text: I also support with organizing and hosting of events for outreach and advocacy purposes. These include, for example, community dinners and cookouts, food system talks, workshop with experts on food conservation, pop-up food distributions or public activism actions. Further we enagage in various networks and with local and national actors, such as the Tipping Point Conference in Helsinki or the Oulu Food Waste Festival, to share our best practices and way of working and to advocate for systemic changes in food policy.

intro: Practicing a culture of creativity, experimentation and care in relation with nature.

body.heading: Purpose
body.text:
At Test Site, people from various backgrounds come together around a shared interest in experimenting with creative ideas for practical sustainability.

There are many projects going on simultaneously, ranging from solar panel construction and beekeeping to a regernative textile garden or a tasteLAB field kitchen. All these projects host open workshops and events to invite others to join and participate in this learning process.

body.heading: Contribution
body.text: I am mainly involved in two projects. First, the gardening project, where we grow vegetables, herbs and flowers in a regenerative way and share the harvest with the community. Additionally, I experiment with plants through natural dyeing processes or sun-printing techniques. I have also tested various recipes involving stinging nettles. Second, the outdoor summer cafe, where we repurposed the tasteLAB field kitchen into a volunteer-run cafe. Through this project we explored alternative ways of organizing ourselves, including shared governance and collective decision-making.

intro: Translating social and ecological principles into actionable, collective practice across sectors and communities.

body.heading: Purpose
body.text:
Our current economic system is primarily concerned with maximizing profits at all costs. This leads not only to the destruction of our planet but also reinforces social inequality.

In response, more than 50 cities and local governments around the world have implemented the Doughnut Economics Framework into their policies and planning processes as a means to reimagine and work towards an alternative economic model that meets the social needs of people within our environmental limits. **Inspired by these examples, we founded DEFI to bring the principles of Doughnut Economics to Finland and put them into practice in our own context.**

body.heading: Tools & Methods
body.text:
Within DEFI, I am mainly involved in developing participatory research tools and methods that engage people in reflecting on the dimensions of the Doughnut framework. By this, we create spaces for people to learn about Doughnut Economics and alternative ways of understanding our economy, but also gather insights into the social and ecological realities of local communities in Otanieme and Espoo. The aim is to better understand where our local context is falling short in meeting social needs and where we are exceeding ecological boundaries.

Specific tools and methods I have co-developed and facilitated, include for example:
→ A Quick Participatory Doughnut Portrait Mapping Canvas to capture community perspectives
→ A Donut Discovery Workshop with 10+ sustainability organisation around Otaniemie to establish partnerships
→ A Step-Inside-the-Donut Workshop with Aalto University students to reflect on our current state of the economy
→ An Interactive Booklet used in a Walkshop with residents of Espoo to learn about lived experiences on social and ecological issues

body.heading: Outcomes
body.text: Through all these projects, we were able to engage and collaborate with a wide range of stakeholders, including local residents, students, sustainability organisations, and city representatives. Ultimately, our goal is to plant the seed for a new economic model in Finland and beyond.
